arxiv-2107-07330.title: DynaDog+T: A Parametric Animal Model for Synthetic Canine Image Generation.
arxiv-2107-07330.creator: Jake Deane 1 Sinéad Kearney 1 Kwang In Kim 2 Darren Cosker 1 CAMERA University of Bath 1 Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology 2 1 (j.deane, d.p.cosker)@bath.ac.uk 2 kimki@unist.ac.kr
arxiv-2107-07330.description: Abstract Synthetic data is becoming increasingly common for training computer vision models for a variety of tasks. Notably, such data has been applied in tasks related to humans such as 3D pose estimation where data is either difficult to create or obtain in realistic settings.

arxiv-2109-12675.title: Bright single-mode RR Lyrae stars: matching Gaia EDR3 with pulsation and evolutionary models
arxiv-2109-12675.creator: Geza Kovacs and Behrooz Karamiqucham
arxiv-2109-12675.description: Abstract We combine observed metallicity, optical and infrared magnitudes with evolutionary and pulsation models to derive average luminosities for 156 156 single-mode RR Lyrae stars. These luminosities are compared with those obtained from the Gaia EDR3 parallaxes, and found in excellent agreement with the high accuracy subsample ( 62 62 stars, with relative parallax errors less than 2 2 %).

arxiv-2211-10831.title: Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures Focus on Slow Features
arxiv-2211-10831.creator: Vlad Sobal 1, Jyothir S V 1, Siddhartha Jalagam 1, Nicolas Carion 2, 2 Meta AI, 3 Prescient Design, Genentech, 4 CIFAR Fellow
arxiv-2211-10831.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vlad Sobal 1, Jyothir S V 1, Siddhartha Jalagam 1, Nicolas Carion 2, 2 Meta AI, 3 Prescient Design, Genentech, 4 CIFAR Fellow. Many common methods for learning a world model for pixel-based environments use generative architectures trained with pixel-level reconstruction objectives. Recently proposed Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) [ 20 ] offer a reconstruction-free alternative.

arxiv-2405-14382.title: Multi-purpose robot for rehabilitation of small diameter water pipes
arxiv-2405-14382.creator: Julien Feiguel, Mouhamed NDiaye, Pascal Chambaud, Adrien Chambellan, Pierre Blanc, Steve Bourgeois, Lucas Labarussiat, Clémence Dubois, Audrey Vigneron, Thomas Desrez, Alain Riwan, and Caroline Vienne
arxiv-2405-14382.description: Abstract Rehabilitating cast iron pipes through lining offers several advantages, including increased durability, reduced water leaks, and minimal disruption. This approach presents a cost-effective and environmentally-friendly solution by sealing cracks and joints, extending the pipeline’s lifespan, and reducing water wastage, all while avoiding the need for trench excavation.

arxiv-2406-05808.title: The Landau–Lifshitz–Bloch equation on polytopal domains: Unique existence and finite element approximation
arxiv-2406-05808.creator: Kim-Ngan Le, Agus L. Soenjaya, Thanh Tran
arxiv-2406-05808.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kim-Ngan Le, Agus L. Soenjaya, Thanh Tran. The Landau–Lifshitz–Bloch equation (LLBE) describes the evolution of the magnetic spin field in ferromagnets at high temperatures. In this paper, we study the numerical approximation of the LLBE in the regime above the Curie temperature on bounded polytopal domains in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , with d ∈ { 1 , 2 , 3 } d\in\{1,2,3\} , allowing for non-convex domains when d = 2 d=2 .

arxiv-2408-06612.title: Double Robust high dimensional alpha test for linear factor pricing model
arxiv-2408-06612.creator: Ping Zhao, Long Feng, Hongfei Wang, Zhaojun Wang
arxiv-2408-06612.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate alpha testing for high-dimensional linear factor pricing models. We propose a spatial sign-based max-type test to handle sparse alternative cases. Additionally, we prove that this test is asymptotically independent of the spatial-sign-based sum-type test proposed by Liu et al. (2023) .

arxiv-2508-08116.title: Handling fabrication defects in hex-grid surface codes
arxiv-2508-08116.creator: Oscar Higgott, Benjamin Anker, Matt McEwen, Dripto M. Debroy
arxiv-2508-08116.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Oscar Higgott, Benjamin Anker, Matt McEwen, Dripto M. Debroy. Recent work has shown that a hexagonal grid qubit layout, with only three couplers per qubit, is sufficient to implement the surface code with performance comparable to that of a traditional four-coupler layout MBG 23 . In this work we propose a method for handling broken qubits and couplers even in hex-grid surface code architectures, using an extension of the LUCI framework DMG+ 24 .

arxiv-2509-24407.title: Q-REACH: Q uantum information R epetition, E rror A nalysis and C orrection using Cac h ing Network
arxiv-2509-24407.creator: Karl C. Linne (Kai Li) 1 , Yuanyuan Li 2 , Debashri Roy 3 , Kaushik Chowdhury 4
arxiv-2509-24407.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Karl C. Linne (Kai Li) 1 , Yuanyuan Li 2 , Debashri Roy 3 , Kaushik Chowdhury 4. Quantum repeaters incorporating quantum memory play a pivotal role in mitigating loss in transmitted quantum information (photons) due to link attenuation over a long-distance quantum communication network.

arxiv-2510-02852.title: Data-Driven Bed Occupancy Planning in Intensive Care Units Using M t / G t / ∞ M_{t}/G_{t}/\infty Queueing Models Journal: Operations Research, Data Analytics and Logistics
arxiv-2510-02852.creator: Maryam Akbari-Moghaddam, Douglas G. Down, Na Li, Catherine Eastwood, Ayman Abou Mehrem, Alexandra Howlett
arxiv-2510-02852.description: Abstract Hospitals struggle to make effective long-term capacity planning decisions for intensive care units (ICUs) under uncertainty in future demand. Admission rates fluctuate over time due to temporal factors, and length of stay (LOS) distributions vary with patient heterogeneity, hospital location, case mix, and clinical practices.

Federated learning (FL) enables decentralized training of machine learning (ML) models across clients without data centralization. Decentralized training, however, introduces a computational burden on client devices.

pmc-10728972.title: Attribution of nosocomial seeding to long-term care facility COVID-19 outbreaks
pmc-10728972.creator: Joe Flannagan, Dimple Y Chudasama, Russell Hope, Simon M Collin, Alex Bhattacharya, Rachel Merrick, Nurin Abdul Aziz, Susan Hopkins, Gavin Dabrera, Theresa Lamagni
pmc-10728972.description: Residents of long-term care facilities (LTCFs) were disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. We matched addresses of cases between March 2020 and June 2021 to reference databases to identify LTCF residents.

pmc-13325550.title: New organic–inorganic rod-like hybrids constructed from Keggin-type polyoxomolybdate and a Cu(ii) dithiocarbamate complex: crystal structure, dye adsorption and antibacterial activity
pmc-13325550.creator: Masoumeh Javanmard, Saeed Farhadi, Michal Dusek, Monika Kucerakova, Keivan Javanmard, Mansoureh Maleki
pmc-13325550.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Novel rod-like organic–inorganic crystalline hybrid materials, namely {Cu[S2CN(CH2Ph)2]2}[H3PMo12O40], (abbreviated as Cu(diBzDTC)2-H3POMo), were synthesized by reacting copper(ii) chloride, in situ prepared N,N-dibenzyldithiocarbamic acid (HdiBzDTC) and H3PMo12O40 polyoxomolybdate (H3POMo) in methanol. The resulting hybrid material was characterized using various techniques, including single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), UV-vis spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with an energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analyzer, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), thermogravimetry and differential thermal (TG/DTA) analyses, elemental analysis, and zeta potential measurements.

pmc-13326058.creator: Rikza Naseer, Anong Tantisuwat
pmc-13326058.description: BackgroundWhile numerous assessment tools exist, their availability in local languages ensures their applicability and requires cross-cultural adaptation. This study aimed to cross-culturally adapt and evaluate psychometric properties of the Urdu version of the Fall Risk Awareness Questionnaire (FRAQ) among older adults, assessing its reliability and preliminary validity in this population.

pmc-13420123.title: Single-tracer [18F]FDG PET quantification of blood–brain barrier permeability and cerebral blood flow: Validation using dual-tracer PET
pmc-13420123.creator: Kevin J Chung, Terry Jones, Yasser G Abdelhafez, Benjamin A Spencer, Javier E Lopez, Lorenzo Nardo, Abhijit J Chaudhari, Audrey P Fan, Ramsey D Badawi, Simon R Cherry, Guobao Wang
pmc-13420123.description: Imaging the blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability of molecular PET tracers may allow pathway-specific assessment of the diverse transport mechanisms expressed at the BBB. However, PET quantification of BBB permeability typically requires dual-tracer protocols involving a flow tracer, increasing methodological complexity and clinical burden.

pmc-13561310.description: ObjectivesTo determine whether bacterial- and viral-associated whole-blood host-response modules discovered in GSE211567 retain their prespecified directions when applied unchanged to two external cohorts, including a second cross-platform cohort, and to quantify their robustness to analytical choices and gene deletion.MethodsFive biologically guided modules were defined and fixed in GSE211567 before external analysis.
